quickAnswer: Buying off-plan property in Türkiye carries higher risk of handover delays, missing occupancy permits (Iskan), and developer financing liens than purchasing a completed resale. Buyers who still choose off-plan should insist on a notarized promise-to-sell contract annotated directly onto the TAPU via [TKGM](https://www.tkgm.gov.tr/e-hizmetler/sik-kullanilanlar/web-tapu) and reviewed by an independent Turkish attorney.

What risks (delivery delays, missing Iskan, title encumbrances) apply to off-plan projects?

Off-plan purchases expose buyers to three primary hazards: construction delays driven by inflation or contractor cash-flow gaps, failure to secure a municipal occupancy permit (yapı kullanma izin belgesi, or Iskan) if the completed structure deviates from approved blueprints, and pre-existing construction mortgages (ipotek) or creditor liens recorded on the parent land parcel.

During construction, units typically carry a construction servitude title (kat irtifakı) rather than full condominium ownership (kat mülkiyeti). If a developer disputes a municipal fine or runs short of capital before obtaining Iskan, buyers can end up living in a finished apartment that still faces higher commercial-rate utility tariffs, mortgage restrictions, and lower resale demand.

body.text: Why must an off-plan promise-to-sell contract be notarized and annotated on the TAPU?

Under Turkish property law, an ordinary sales contract signed in a developer's showroom does not transfer ownership or block the land owner from reselling or mortgaging the same unit to a third party. A promise-to-sell agreement (taşınmaz satış vaadi sözleşmesi) becomes legally enforceable only when executed before a Turkish notary public under the [Union of Notaries of Türkiye (TNB)](https://portal.tnb.org.tr/sayfalar/noterlikkanunu.aspx) framework and annotated (şerh) onto the land registry record at [TKGM](https://www.tkgm.gov.tr/e-hizmetler/sik-kullanilanlar/web-tapu).

Notarization and TAPU annotation protect the buyer's priority for five years against subsequent third-party buyers or developer creditors. Before booking a [TNB notary appointment](https://portal.tnb.org.tr/Sayfalar/BasvuruHiz.aspx), hire a Baro-verified attorney via the [Union of Turkish Bar Associations (TBB)](https://barobirlik.org.tr/AvukatArama) to confirm whether the developer owns the land outright or operates under a land-share construction agreement (kat karşılığı inşaat sözleşmesi) with separate landowners.
When is a completed resale with full Iskan safer for citizenship or rental?

A completed resale with verified kat mülkiyeti and full Iskan is substantially safer whenever your timeline is tied to residency, Turkish citizenship-by-investment filings, or immediate rental cash flow. Because the unit already exists, your independent attorney, civil engineer, and licensed SPK appraiser can verify exact square footage, building-code compliance under [AFAD's 2018 TBDY standards](https://www.afad.gov.tr/turkiye-bina-deprem-yonetmeligi), and true neighborhood rent comparables before funds move.

Completed apartments also eliminate the hidden gap between optimistic sales brochures and real-world site management (aidat) costs. You can walk the actual street at night, check elevator maintenance, inspect basement parking for dampness, and confirm that existing residents have active residential utility meters.
How do you inspect a developer's past completed projects?

Evaluating a developer's real track record requires visiting two or three buildings they delivered three to five years ago—unannounced and without a sales representative steering the conversation. Speaking briefly with site managers or residents reveals far more about build quality, post-handover repairs, and Iskan delivery speed than any marketing render.

items: Visit at least two completed projects from the same developer and inspect facade weathering, lobby upkeep, and underground garage waterproofing.
Ask current residents or the building manager (site yönetimi) how long after key handover the developer obtained full Iskan.
Verify through your independent attorney whether the developer's corporate entity has open commercial lawsuits, tax liens, or unpaid subcontractor disputes.
Compare promised completion dates on older brochures against actual occupancy dates.
Confirm that escrow or milestone payments tie strictly to verifiable construction stages rather than fixed calendar dates.

faq.q: Is an ordinary developer sales contract signed in English legally binding in Türkiye?
faq.a: An unnotarized contract signed in a sales office may establish a personal debt claim for refunds, but it cannot compel TAPU title transfer or stop a third-party sale. Official real estate promise-to-sell contracts must be executed in Turkish before a notary with a sworn translator.

faq.q: How long does a TAPU annotation (şerh) stay valid on an off-plan property?
faq.a: A promise-to-sell annotation recorded on the land registry remains legally protective against third parties for five years from the date of annotation under Turkish law.

faq.q: Can you get a mortgage or citizenship with an off-plan contract?
faq.a: Banks rarely finance uncompleted foreign-buyer purchases without Iskan. Citizenship-by-investment applications can use notarized promise-to-sell contracts only when strict statutory payment, valuation, and annotation rules are met—always confirm eligibility with a licensed Turkish attorney.

faq.q: What is the difference between kat irtifakı and kat mülkiyeti on a TAPU?
faq.a: Kat irtifakı is a construction servitude title issued before building completion and municipal Iskan sign-off. Kat mülkiyeti is full condominium ownership granted once the building passes final municipal inspection.

faq.q: Should I visit a developer's past projects with a real estate agent?
faq.a: It is best to inspect past completed buildings independently—or with your own neutral ground coordinator and engineer—so residents and site managers speak candidly about maintenance and handover history.
